FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

After one of the most memorable wins in their recent Premier League history last weekend, Leeds look to garner the momentum into another positive result against newly-promoted Coventry. 

Match News and Current Form

Leeds produced something of a shock result last weekend as they downed Chelsea 4-1 at Stamford Bridge to secure back-to-back Premier League victories. The Whites sit just a point adrift of the top five pre-round and could bridge that gap by securing a third top-flight win in succession for the first time since May 2021, while boss Daniel Farke has never achieved such a feat in the Premier League. An impressive ten-match unbeaten run in competitive action at Elland Road (W6, D4) suggests they’re good value to do exactly that, while Farke’s unbeaten managerial record when hosting Coventry (W2, D2) only serves to further boost belief.

Coventry are excelling in their first season back in the Premier League after a 20+ year absence, with last weekend’s 3-2 victory over Crystal Palace solidifying their mid-table standing. Most of their good work has been done at home, where each of their last three victories arrived, while on the road they’ve lost back-to-back games by the same 3-1 scoreline. This game looks set to be decided one way or another too, given none of Coventry’s first 11 league games ended in stalemate (W4, L7), which is their joint-longest run in history without a draw from the start of a league season and could become an outright record here.

Head-to-Head History

Leeds have lost just one of their last 23 home league games against Coventry (W16, D6) and are unbeaten in the last eight Premier League meetings (W4, D4).

Win Probability
Opta by StatsPerform
Hot Stats and Streaks

None of Leeds’ home league games this term produced a goal in the opening 30 minutes.

Six of Leeds’ last seven Premier League matches produced 4+ yellow cards.

Five of Coventry’s last six league matches produced over 3.5 goals.

Coventry scored all three of their away league goals this season in the second half. 

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Leeds’ Noah Okafor has scored ten of his 12 Premier League goals across his last 17 appearances, with four of his last five strikes arriving in the second half. Tatsuhiro Sakamoto was on target for Coventry last weekend with his fifth successive club goal to arrive before half-time.

Leeds have no fresh concerns, but Coventry’s Caleb Yirenkyi missed the win over Palace, a game in which Taiwo Awoniyi was withdrawn with injury.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

Leeds are in phenomenal form at Elland Road, and with Coventry struggling on the road, a home win by a -1 handicap may not be too far-fetched here.

Author: Chris Wilson
